citation: Lang, L., Torgesen, J., Vogel, W., Chanter, C., Lefsky, E., & Petscher, Y. (2009). Exploring the relative effectiveness of reading interventions for high school students. Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness, 2(2), 149-175. https://doi.org/10.1080/19345740802641535
report_number: Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness, 2(2), 149-175
design: Year-long (2006-2007, Year 3 of a 3-year project) student-level RCT. 1,265 struggling grade-9 readers (reduced analytic sample 1,197 after outlier removal) in 87-89 classes taught by 31 teachers across 7 high schools in one large Florida district (Seminole County). Students screened on prior-year FCAT-SSS Reading into High Risk (Achievement Level 1, below 4th-grade reading, n=385) and Moderate Risk (Level 2, 4th-6th grade reading, n=812), then randomly assigned WITHIN school and WITHIN risk level (Latin-square) to one of FOUR 90-min intensive reading interventions: THREE program arms -- READ 180, REACH System 2002, and RISE (Reading Intervention through Strategy Enhancement) -- each with publisher/developer-led teacher professional development plus school reading-coach coaching, versus the school-designed 'business as usual' control SOAR (School Offered Accelerated Reading). Outcome: reading achievement = FCAT Developmental Scale Score (DSS) gain (posttest 2006-07 minus pretest 2005-06) on the criterion-referenced Florida state reading test. Analysis: 2x4 (Risk x Intervention) linear mixed model with random classroom coefficients on 10 multiply-imputed datasets; SOAR is the reference. The Risk x Intervention interaction was significant (F=4.05, p<.05), so impacts are reported separately by risk group. Three program-vs-control arms = registry rows 67 (READ 180), 68 (REACH), 69 (RISE) -- though arm-to-row name mapping is by program; see notes.
problems: Arm/row mapping by program name is inferred (registry gives 3 arms sharing one control; the paper's three programs are READ 180, REACH, RISE -- assigned to rows 67/68/69 respectively in author/program order; if the meta-analysts ordered arms differently the row labels may need swapping, but all three g values are present). Significant Risk x Intervention interaction means there is NO single pooled program-vs-control g for the full struggling-reader sample; the paper only reports impacts split by risk subgroup. I therefore extract BOTH risk subgroups per arm (is_full_sample=false for all; these are randomized subgroups defined by pre-assignment risk strata). The MODERATE-RISK contrast is the study's headline/abstract result (Glass adj delta = .30 for READ 180, .27 for RISE, both reliable; REACH n.s.) and is marked outcome_role=primary; the HIGH-RISK contrast (no program beat SOAR; deltas -0.19/-0.27/-0.06) is marked outcome_role=subgroup/secondary. The paper reports Glass's adjusted delta (control/SOAR SD); g here is recomputed as the small-sample-corrected pooled-SD SMD from Table 2 gain means/SDs (matches the paper's deltas to within rounding and matches Table 3 model fitted-mean differences). Clustering: students nested in classrooms; unconditional ICC=0.24 (24% of FCAT-gain variance between classrooms). The mixed model accounts for clustering, but the g values here are computed from student-level means/SDs, so cluster_adjusted=false and ICC + classroom count are recorded for central Hedges-2007 correction. Per-cell (risk x arm) classroom counts are not reported (total ~87 classes / 31 teachers across 8 cells); n_clusters recorded at study level (87). Note: SIGN -- positive g favors the TPD program over the SOAR business-as-usual control.

effect_sizes.arm_label: READ 180 (Scholastic) vs SOAR business-as-usual control -- Moderate Risk (Level 2) grade-9 struggling readers
effect_sizes.test_name: FCAT-SSS Reading, Developmental Scale Score (DSS) gain
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (end of grade 9, spring 2007; single end-of-year wave)
effect_sizes.g_method: d = (M_t - M_c)/s_pooled from Table 2 moderate-risk gain means/SDs (READ180 104.53/126.16 vs SOAR 69.85/119.57; s_pooled=122.95); g = J*d, J=0.9982. Matches paper's Glass adj delta .30 (control-SD standardization) and Table 3 fitted-mean diff (104.60-69.00=35.6) /s_pooled = 0.289.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.164 Table 2; p.167 Table 3; abstract p.149; pp.169-170
effect_sizes.notes: Headline/abstract result (delta=.30, F=6.31, p=.029): READ 180 significantly outperformed SOAR among moderate-risk readers. Outcome is the gain score (pretest covaried via gain; paper argues residualized change unnecessary given low pretest variability). is_full_sample=false: moderate-risk is a randomized pre-assignment risk stratum, not the whole struggling-reader sample (interaction was significant so no pooled effect is reported).
